topic.readerProblem: A marketer or SEO lead wants to know what Semrush's AI Visibility Toolkit actually is, what it measures, what it really costs and whether to buy it or skip it.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines recommend a brand; the page explains where a suite add-on's tracking fits versus a one-off audit and where the crawler-access data from AEOeye's study applies.

assessment: The page defines the toolkit from Semrush's own knowledge base, lists its six components, the score definition and refresh cadence, and builds a price table from the pricing page and knowledge base, with per-prompt arithmetic and a bundle comparison against Semrush One. It states the inconsistencies Semrush itself shows (engine list, user price, trial) instead of picking one, and says what the pages do not document. It rests on Semrush's public pages only, uses AEOeye's crawler study with its n and caveat, and does not claim hands-on testing, accuracy or ranking outcomes.

sources.supports: Toolkit components, AI Visibility Score definition, refresh cadence, $99 price and included limits, no free trial, extra prompts $60/50, extra domain $99, sub-user license $99, ChatGPT and Google AI Mode named.

Base $99/mo per domain billed annually; 25 custom prompts; mentions from ChatGPT, Google AI, Gemini and Perplexity; additional users from $45/mo; Base Report $10/mo, Pro Report $20/mo with white-labeling; Enterprise custom.
SEO plan $117.33/mo annual ($139 monthly); Starter $165.17 annual ($199 monthly) 50 prompts; Pro+ $248.17 ($299) 100 prompts; Advanced $455.67 ($549) 200 prompts.
Feature page names 'ChatGPT, AI Overviews, and other LLMs' without listing engines.
Search Console generative AI performance report shows impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode; rolled out to all websites worldwide as of August 31, 2026.
OtterlyAI Lite $29/month (15 prompts), Standard $189/month (100 prompts) on monthly billing; free trial offered.
Profound pricing page: free Trial (50 prompts run daily for 7 days across ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews) and a custom-priced Enterprise plan.
Google says no new machine-readable files, AI text files or special markup are needed to appear in Google Search including its generative AI capabilities.
